key_insight: SPARKLING enables stable width expansion mid-training by jointly preserving the network's signal (activations/gradients) when new channels are added and introducing controlled symmetry breaking so new parameters become useful rather than redundant.
problem_solved: How to safely and efficiently increase model width during the middle of pre-training—maximizing compute savings from progressive learning—without causing the severe instabilities and collapse that naive width expansion produces.
method: Signal preservation: initialize and rescale new channels so activations and gradients remain consistent with the pre-expanded model (e.g., parameter copying + calibrated scaling of new weights/normalization).
Symmetry breaking: inject small, structured perturbations or learnable diversifying factors to newly added units so they rapidly specialize instead of staying redundant copies.
Stabilization schedule: combine a width-growth curriculum (timing and fraction of channels added) with short warmup and normalization adjustments to ensure smooth adaptation.
impact: Makes width-progressive learning practical beyond very early training stages, enabling large compute and time savings for practitioners who want to grow models dynamically. It broadens progressive scaling strategies beyond depth-only methods and reduces the cost of pre-training large models.

paper_title: SPARKLING: Balancing Signal Preservation and Symmetry Breaking for Width-Progressive Learning
paper_authors: Qifan Yu, Xinyu Ma, Zhijian Zhuo, Minrui Wang, Deyi Liu
